description: Factual questions put to Alice (the example alice-s-adventures-in-wonderland, English text) to check that the answers are right. expectedOutput is the right answer, read by the accuracy judge (evals/accuracy-judge.json); passageQuotes are phrases of the book that hold it. 20 questions, one from each of 20 evenly spaced passages (passages 1 to 104), written on 26 November 2026 before any search or reply, and not changed after.

items.input: As you fell down the well, you took a jar from one of the shelves. What was written on it, and what was inside?
items.expectedOutput: The jar was labelled ORANGE MARMALADE, and it was empty.
passageQuotes: but to her great disappointment it was empty

items.input: After drinking from the little bottle you were the right size for the garden door. What had you forgotten?
items.expectedOutput: The little golden key, left on the glass table, which she could then no longer reach.
passageQuotes: she found she had forgotten the little golden key

items.input: What made you shrink so quickly just before you fell into the water?
items.expectedOutput: The fan she was holding (the White Rabbit's fan).
passageQuotes: the cause of this was the fan she was holding

items.input: You were all wet after the pool. What did the Dodo propose to get you dry?
items.expectedOutput: A Caucus-race.
passageQuotes: the best thing to get us dry would be a Caucus-race

items.input: When the White Rabbit called out to you angrily, who did he take you for, and what did he tell you to fetch?
items.expectedOutput: He took her for Mary Ann, his housemaid, and told her to fetch him a pair of gloves and a fan.
passageQuotes: Why, Mary Ann, what are you doing out here?

items.input: While you were stuck in the Rabbit's house, who was to be sent down the chimney?
items.expectedOutput: Bill.
passageQuotes: Bill's to go down

items.input: What was the Caterpillar smoking, and what was the first thing it asked you?
items.expectedOutput: A long hookah; it asked her "Who are you?".
passageQuotes: quietly smoking a long hookah

items.input: Why did the Pigeon take you for a serpent, and what did you answer that you were?
items.expectedOutput: Because of her very long neck (it also asked about eggs); she answered that she was a little girl.
passageQuotes: never one with such a neck as that

items.input: In the Duchess's kitchen, what was there certainly too much of, and in what?
items.expectedOutput: Too much pepper, in the soup.
passageQuotes: too much pepper in that soup

items.input: Who did the Cheshire Cat say lived in the two directions it pointed to?
items.expectedOutput: A Hatter in one direction and a March Hare in the other, both mad.
passageQuotes: lives a Hatter: and in that direction

items.input: What was strange about the watch at the tea party?
items.expectedOutput: It told the day of the month, not what o'clock it was.
passageQuotes: It tells the day of the month

items.input: When you walked away from the tea party, what were the others doing with the Dormouse?
items.expectedOutput: They were trying to put the Dormouse into the teapot.
passageQuotes: they were trying to put the Dormouse into the teapot

items.input: In the Queen's game of croquet, what were used as balls and as mallets?
items.expectedOutput: Live hedgehogs as balls and live flamingoes as mallets.
passageQuotes: the balls were live hedgehogs, the mallets live flamingoes

items.input: When the Duchess took your arm again, what did you suppose had made her so savage in the kitchen?
items.expectedOutput: The pepper.
passageQuotes: perhaps it was only the pepper that had made her so savage

items.input: Whom did the Queen order to take you to the Mock Turtle, and what was that creature doing when you found it?
items.expectedOutput: The Gryphon, which was lying fast asleep in the sun.
passageQuotes: They very soon came upon a Gryphon, lying fast asleep in the sun

items.input: In the dance that the Mock Turtle and the Gryphon described, what do you throw as far out to sea as you can?
items.expectedOutput: The lobsters.
passageQuotes: as far out to sea as you can

items.input: What did the Mock Turtle say about the verses you were reciting about the Owl and the Panther?
items.expectedOutput: That it was useless to repeat them without explaining them: by far the most confusing thing he had ever heard.
passageQuotes: by far the most confusing thing I ever heard

items.input: At the trial, what happened to the Hatter when the Queen asked for the list of the singers at the last concert?
items.expectedOutput: He trembled so much that he shook both his shoes off.
passageQuotes: that he shook both his shoes off

items.input: Which rule did the King read to make you leave the court, and what did you say about it?
items.expectedOutput: Rule Forty-two, that all persons more than a mile high must leave the court; she said it was not a regular rule, he had just invented it.
passageQuotes: All persons more than a mile high to leave the court

items.input: Who woke you at the end, and what did that person tell you to go and do?
items.expectedOutput: Her sister, who told her to run in to her tea because it was getting late.
passageQuotes: but now run in to your tea
